newsitem.title: USA: Watson Meperidine tablets get FDA nod.
newsitem.headline: Watson Meperidine tablets get FDA nod.

text.p: Watson Pharmaceuticals Inc said Monday its Royce Laboratories Inc unit had received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for its abbreviated new drug application for Meperidine tablets, to treat pain.
Meperidine is the off-patent equivalent of Sanofi Winthrops's Demerol, which is used in the treatment of severe to moderately severe pain, Watson said. Sanofi Winthrops is part of Elf Sanofi SA.
Watson makes and sells off-patent medications and branded pharmaceutical products.
Approval was granted for tablets of 50- and 100-milligram strength, it said. Watson said it planned to launch the product during the third quarter.
"Meperidine is Watson's first schedule II narcotic ANDA approval and complements our existing analgesic product line," said Allen Chao, chairman and chief executive officer.
Watson estimated the product's market size was about $20 million.
